My grandfather opened this cafe in Ljubljana in 1952, so it has been in our family for more than seventy years. I have worked here since I was sixteen. That is thirty-four years now. The tables are the same, and the old coffee machine has survived three generations of my family. Some customers have come here every morning for decades. Mr. Novak, for example, has had the same table by the window since 1980. Tourists sometimes ask me: Why don't you change anything? My answer is simple. People don't come here for new things. They come because some things last.

I have supported Hajduk Split since I was six years old. My father took me to my first game in 1961, at the old stadium in the city. Since 1979 the team has played at Poljud, by the sea, and I have had the same seat there for more than forty years. I have seen good decades and bad decades. We haven't won the league for a long time, and my wife says I am crazy. Maybe she is right. But I have never missed a derby against Dinamo since 1985. Some things a man does not stop, not even at seventy-one.

In 1968 Marko moved into a small apartment near the Peristyle. Then, for many years, he taught at a school in Split and walked home through the Roman streets. After that, in 1979, the palace became a UNESCO World Heritage Site. At that point tourists started to arrive, more every summer. Today he has lived there for more than fifty years, and he still knows every neighbor.
